video.title: Allah’s Mercy Is Greater Than All Your Sins
video.creator: FreeQuranEducation

summary.headline: All three claims trace to authentic Qur'anic and Hadith sources.
summary.note: This video relays three well-known Hadith Qudsi accurately. No weak or fabricated narrations were detected, and one claim is grounded directly in the Qur'an.

claims.originalQuote: Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night and asks who is calling upon Him so He can answer.
claims.normalizedClaim: Allah descends to the lowest heaven during the last third of the night to answer the supplications of His servants.

sahih.excerpt: Our Lord, the Blessed, the Superior, comes every night down on the nearest Heaven to us when the last third of the night remains...
Allah descends every night to the lowest heaven when one-third of the first part of the night is over...
The Lord Almighty descends to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains...
Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, descends to the lowest heaven...

hasan.excerpt: Our Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven...
Allah descends to the lowest heaven...
hasan.gradingNote: Hasan. Lower entailment as it focuses purely on the descent rather than the call/response.

claims.originalQuote: Nothing can change your destiny or Qadar except your dua.
claims.normalizedClaim: Supplication (Dua) is the only thing that can alter the Divine Decree (Qadar).

hasan.excerpt: Nothing turns back the Decree except supplication, and nothing increases life span except righteousness.
Nothing repels the decree except supplication...
A man is deprived of provision because of a sin he commits. Nothing repels the decree except supplication...
Caution does not save from the decree, but supplication benefits against what has been decreed and what has not been decreed.
hasan.gradingNote: Graded Hasan by some scholars; corroborates the main claim indirectly.

hasan.excerpt: Supplication is beneficial regarding things that have already happened and things that have not yet happened.
hasan.gradingNote: Hasan; provides partial entailment (60%) to the overarching concept of Dua actively affecting decree without using the explicit 'nothing changes' language.

claims.originalQuote: Dua is the essence of worship.
claims.normalizedClaim: Supplication (Dua) is intrinsically linked to, or constitutes the core essence of, worship in Islam.

quran.excerpt: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.
quran.gradingNote: Definitive (qaṭ'ī). Establishes Dua as practically synonymous with worship.

sahih.excerpt: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Supplication is worship.
Supplication is worship. Then he recited: 'And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will answer you.'
The Messenger of Allah said, 'Indeed, supplication is worship.'

hasan.excerpt: The Messenger of Allah said: 'There is nothing more honorable to Allah than supplication.'
hasan.gradingNote: Hasan (Darussalam). Provides partial entailment (65%) indicating the high overarching status of Dua in worship.

hasan.excerpt: Supplication is the essence of worship.
hasan.gradingNote: Often cited as the exact quote, though its specific chain is considered Da'if (weak) by some, it heavily entails the original quote contextually.

video.title: We've all done this — a friend stops a gossip session before it starts
video.creator: Browniesaadi

summary.headline: All three claims align with established Qur'anic verses and authenticated Hadith on backbiting, talebearing, and the discord they cause.
summary.note: This skit accurately reflects mainstream Islamic teaching: gheebah (backbiting) and namimah (talebearing) are both classified as major sins, and namimah is repeatedly singled out — including in a hadith about punishment in the grave — as a cause of broken relationships and fitna. One nuance worth flagging: scholars recognize six narrow, necessity-based exceptions to the backbiting prohibition (e.g. reporting oppression to someone who can fix it, seeking a religious ruling). The video states the rule as an absolute, which is the common simplified framing but not the complete fiqh picture.

claims.originalQuote: You're about to commit a major sin in Islam. Gossiping... is actually a major sin.
claims.normalizedClaim: Speaking about someone behind their back in a way they would dislike (gheebah/backbiting) is treated as a major sin in Islam, even when the statement is factually true.

quran.excerpt: And do not backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it.
quran.gradingNote: Definitive (qaṭ'ī) — established Qur'anic text; the primary proof-text scholars cite when discussing gheebah.

quran.excerpt: Woe to every scorner and slanderer.
quran.gradingNote: Definitive Qur'anic text, though 'humazah/lumazah' is a broader term for defamation by word and gesture, not gheebah specifically — Ibn Kathir links it to the same family of sins.

sahih.excerpt: Do you know what backbiting is? ... It is to mention your brother in a way he dislikes. ... If what you say about him is true, you have backbitten him; if it is not true, you have slandered him.
sahih.gradingNote: Sahih, recorded by Muslim — the foundational hadith that defines gheebah.

sahih.excerpt: The real bankrupt of my Ummah is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting, and charity, but comes having abused this one, slandered that one... so his good deeds are given away, and if they run out, the sins of those he wronged are loaded onto him.
sahih.gradingNote: Sahih; establishes the severity of backbiting via its cost on Judgment Day, supporting the 'major sin' classification rather than defining the act itself.

sahih.excerpt: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say good or remain silent.
sahih.gradingNote: Muttafaq 'Alayh; a general principle about guarding speech rather than a direct ruling on gheebah — supports but doesn't independently establish the claim.

hasan.reference: Riyad al-Salihin, Ch. 256 (Imam Nawawi, summarizing scholarly ijma')
hasan.narrator: Scholarly consensus, not a hadith narration
hasan.excerpt: Backbiting is permissible only for a legitimate Shari'ah purpose unattainable without it — six such purposes: reporting an injustice, seeking help to correct a wrong, requesting a religious ruling, warning Muslims of harm, naming an open sinner, and identification by a known trait.
hasan.gradingNote: Not a hadith itself but a near-unanimous fiqh ruling. It doesn't contradict the prohibition — it qualifies it. Included because the video states the rule as an unqualified blanket prohibition, which omits these recognized exceptions.

claims.originalQuote: Telling people what others said about them to cause fitna is actually a major sin.
claims.normalizedClaim: Carrying tales between people, specifically repeating what one person said about another with the effect or intent of stirring conflict (namimah) major sin in Islam.

quran.excerpt: A habitual faultfinder, going about with malicious gossip (namīm).
quran.gradingNote: Definitive Qur'anic text naming namimah explicitly as a trait of a corrupt character.

sahih.excerpt: The qattat (talebearer) will not enter Paradise.
sahih.gradingNote: Muttafaq 'Alayh — agreed upon by Bukhari and Muslim, the highest tier of authenticity. 'Qattat' is the classical term for someone who relays what was said in order to cause harm.

sahih.excerpt: These two are being punished, but not for anything difficult to avoid. One of them did not guard himself from his urine; the other used to go about with namimah, to cause enmity between people.
sahih.gradingNote: Muttafaq 'Alayh; one of the two men punished in his grave is explicitly described as a talebearer who stirred enmity between friends — directly matches the video's description.

sahih.excerpt: ...going about between people, spreading words to corrupt their relationships.
sahih.gradingNote: Graded Sahih by Al-Albani; from Bukhari's separate compilation on manners, slightly outside the two Sahihayn but still authenticated.

hasan.reference: Sahih al-Targhib wa't-Tarhib 2824 (compiled & graded by Al-Albani)
hasan.excerpt: The worst of Allah's slaves are the talebearers, who cause separation between those who love each other and seek out faults for the blameless.
hasan.gradingNote: Hasan; graded by Al-Albani from multiple supporting chains. Closely matches the video's description of namimah as deliberately stirring conflict.
